# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

## Goal (user story)

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared-market phase alternation is visible (whose turn) and input is gated to the active player; AI turn is animated with a brief delay.
- [ ] **AC3:** Every competitive action that uses a core-engine animation helper is wired with SFX (via helper `soundManager`/`sfx` params or `GameEventEmitter`/`SoundManager`); SFX keys follow `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention; reduced-motion and mute respected.
- [ ] **AC4:** Build + unit tests pass; smoke browser coverage for the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScene.ts` — Competitive scene (owner-coloured street, phase alternation, SFX).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveRenderer.ts` — Owner-colour helpers (tinting by ownerId).
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` source of truth for SFX keys.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene.browser.test.ts` — Smoke/browser coverage.

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode (engine-only; rendering deferred here per AC5)
- Siblings: state, phase, income/events, AI strategy, Monte Carlo (engine foundation this child renders)
- AGENTS.md §8 — Every action with animation must have SFX

# Add a Charity Shop business card (MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. The producer has specified the card's core economy (1.5 income/turn, 0.15 reputation/turn, cost 3 at the pre-scale convention), and this work adds the card to the pool so players gain an early reputation-leaning Culture business at tier 2.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.
- **As a player**, I expect the Charity Shop to participate in Culture adjacency synergy like other Culture businesses (Bookshop, Craft Shop), so I can cluster it with my Culture cards.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect the new card to be a first-class registered template — present in the CSV, the tier/progression system, generated metadata and card art — with all template-count and consistency tests updated rather than special-cased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath` empty (standalone), `maxLevel = 0`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`. (**Producer-accepted variance, 2026-10-01:** the card is standalone — `upgradePath` empty and `maxLevel = 0` — matching the repo convention for standalone businesses (Craft Shop, Pharmacy, Grand Hotel); the earlier `upgradePath = Charity Shop` / `maxLevel = 1` wording was self-contradictory since no matching upgrade card exists.)
2. **Registered template.** The card is loaded by `MainStreetCards.ts` as a business template, is available at tier 2 through the tier/`CARD_TIER_MAP` progression, and appears in the business deck built by `createBusinessDeck()`.
3. **Generated metadata and art.** `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` lists `biz-charity-shop` under `expandedCardIds.business`, and `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` produces `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg`; both are committed.
4. **Tests.** Automated tests assert the Charity Shop's `cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `synergyTypes` and `tier`, and every hardcoded count affected by adding one business template is updated:
   - business-template count `30 → 31` in `game-state.test.ts` (`BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT`), `expanded-card-pool.test.ts`, `group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` (test title/comment too), and the `createBusinessDeck(1).length` assertions in the `group-b`…`group-f` expansion tests;
   - aggregate pool totals in `meta-progression.test.ts`: tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` `173 → 174` and unique base-id `allBaseIds.size` `165 → 166`;
   - the hardcoded tier-2 synergy snapshot in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` becomes `{ Commerce: 2, Service: 1, Culture: 1 }`.
   The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (business table, deck-size/expansion counts, synergy-type coverage) and any relevant README or docs-site entries. **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): all coin/reputation CSV values are integers at 100× the design scale — `cost 300`, `baseIncome 150`, `reputationPerTurn 15`. No fractional values anywhere in the CSV.
- **Ongoing cost convention** (CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE): businesses pay ¼ of purchase price per turn (min 25), so `ongoingCost = 75`; the card is charged this while in hand or on the street.
- **Card text must match data** (`card-text-data-consistency` test): the `description` reputation figure must equal the `reputationPerTurn` value and the synergy sentence must match the Culture synergy.
- **Tier-2 synergy balance** (`tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`, ≤2× ratio): tier 2 becomes Commerce 2 / Service 1 / Culture 1 — ratio 2.0, which passes.
- **Tier family balance** (`tier-family-balance.test.ts`, ≤46% per family): tier 2 business share becomes 4/22 ≈ 18.2% — passes.
- **Producer-specified cost override:** the balance curve (`tier*2 + 2 + baseIncome*4 + …`) would price this card higher than 300; the producer's explicit `cost 3` (300) takes precedence and is recorded as a deliberate manual override, not a curve result.

## Existing state

- There is **no** charity shop / thrift / op-shop card in `card-data.csv` or `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; this is a net-new template.
- The pool currently has **30 business templates**; tier 2 contains Hardware Store (Service), Pawn Shop (Commerce) and Boutique (Commerce).
- Business cards are generic CSV-driven templates; `MainStreetCards.ts` parses rows, and per-tier registration is derived from the CSV `tier` column (`CARD_TIER_MAP`) — no bespoke TypeScript class is needed.
- Tests hardcode both the business-template count (`30`) **and aggregate pool totals** (tier-12 cumulative `173`, unique base-id set `165`), and `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` enumerates every non-baseline business id (currently 26 business ids; with the 4 tier-1 baseline business ids the total is 30) — all must be updated. `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` also hardcodes the per-tier synergy snapshot.
- Business card art resolves through `card-art-map.json` with a generic `Fallback` sprite when a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite is absent.

## Desired change

Add the Charity Shop as a tier-2 Culture business template with the values in AC1, regenerate the derived metadata and SVG card artifacts, update the hardcoded business-count assertions and the catalog documentation, and add/extend tests asserting the new card's economy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — add the `biz-charity-shop` business row.
- `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — regenerate via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` (business id list grows 26 → 27).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg` — generated by `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — add the card to the tier-2 business table; update the two deck-size tables (Business 30 → 31, business cards 90 → 93), the expansion summary (Business 30 → 31, total 157 → 158, net +142 → +143) and the synergy-type coverage table (Culture single 4 → 5; Culture total 10 → 11).
- `tests/main-street/game-state.test.ts` — `BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and wording/comment).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and test description).
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts`, `group-c-investment-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-e-upgrade-cards-expansion.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — `createBusinessDeck(1).length` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` 173 → 174 (test title/comment too) and `allBaseIds.size` 165 → 166.
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — extend the hardcoded sparse-tier snapshot for `'tier-2'` with `Culture: 1` (and update the header comment); optionally add a Charity Shop synergy assertion.
- `tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-svg-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tier-family-balance.test.ts` — driven by the regenerated artifacts/CSV; verify they pass.
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — verifies card text matches data; passes once `description`/`art_notes` match the values in AC1.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — add a Special Cases note for the producer's manual cost override (if the balance doc is maintained against the CSV).

## Related work

> The `CG-` ids below are from the legacy Tableau-Card-Engine (core) worklog; the same content was migrated to this repo under the `MS-` prefix (see the migration comment on this item).

- `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated producer note; establishes the ×100 value convention for business cards).
- `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
- `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (¼ purchase price, min 25).
- `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text.
- `CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB` — tier synergy-type balance rule (constrains tier-2 placement).
- `CG-0MT3C744B009DS84` / `CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143` — 12-tier progression and family rebalance.
- Automated related-work report: `CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY` (Main Street: design 50+ new cards), `CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA` (synergy icons in help panel).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q2):** synergy type is **Culture** (a charity shop might thematically read as Commerce; overridden by the producer's answer).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q3; wording corrected on acceptance of the AC1 variance 2026-10-01):** **tier 2, standalone** (`upgradePath` empty, `maxLevel = 0`, no upgrade chain).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q1):** 1.5 is **gross** `baseIncome`; the standard 75 ongoing cost applies on top (net 0.75/turn).
- **Assumption (not explicitly confirmed; low risk):** `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, and house-style `description`/`art_notes` text; the card uses the generic fallback sprite until dedicated art is supplied.
- **Risk:** hardcoded business counts **and aggregate pool totals** are spread across many tests; missing one turns the suite red — the count updates are the largest part of the change.
- **Risk:** regenerating `expanded-card-manifest.json` and SVG artifacts produces large/generated diffs; regenerate via the documented scripts rather than hand-editing.
- **Scope-creep guard:** dedicated 1024×1024 artwork for the card is **out of scope**; if wanted, record it as a linked follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — 1.5 is gross `baseIncome`; `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net 0.75/turn. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4` on this item.
- **Q2: Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): C** — `Culture`. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Q3: Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — `tier = 2`, standalone. The literal `upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1` values carried in from the originating intake were incorrect for a standalone card and were corrected to `upgradePath` empty / `maxLevel = 0`; the producer **accepted this variance on 2026-10-01** (see the producer acceptance comment on this item). Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Note:** these answers were carried over from the originating (core-repo) intake; the producer should confirm them alongside the corrected paths/counts at the next review.
- **Non-blocking assumptions:** `id`/`name`/`description`/`art_notes` and fallback-art usage were proposed in the questions comment and **not corrected** by the producer; they are treated as accepted defaults unless the producer objects.

# Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw)

**Summary:** Add the engine logic for the Investor's free market re-roll: per-turn state tracking, the bias-aware draw algorithm, and the integration with the existing market refill path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform one coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it advances the per-turn escalation counter (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a 75% chance to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space synergyTypes; event targetSynergy/effect; staff allowedBusinessTypes overlap with the hosting business's synergy types).
- The biased draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed produces same-game determinism.
- `refillSingleRowMarket` is parameterised to accept the bias/relevance pool; the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- The bias draw preserves the >=1-business row composition invariant.

**Parent Coverage:** Implements parent AC2 (One free re-roll per turn) and parent AC3 (Relevance bias).

**Minimal Implementation:**
- Add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` to state types
- Reset flag at `WeekStart`
- Implement `canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`
- Implement bias-aware draw in `refillSingleRowMarket`
- Wire up the bias detection (hosting business synergy types overlap)

**Dependencies:** Add Investor card to catalog (CSV + types + parsing)

**Deliverables:** Engine functions, state field, bias draw algorithm, WeekStart reset.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`

# Core scaffold template Pages base

**Parent:** MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 · `task` · cross-repo

**Goal.** Update the core scaffold template so that a future
`npm run scaffold` does not clobber the Pages base path in
`./vite.config.ts`.

**Why.** `./vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED from
`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and says so in its banner. Without the
template change the Pages fix regresses the next time the repo is re-scaffolded.

**Cross-repo process.** The edit lands in the `core` submodule checkout
(`/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`), which is a separate repository
with its own worklog and its own build → test → commit gates. Per the approved
plan option (a), a `CG-…` work item is raised there, the change is committed under
that item, and only then is the `core` submodule pointer bumped here. No files
under `.pi/`, `skill/` or `command/` are touched in either repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` emits the same generic production-base derivation as `./vite.config.ts` (package-name derived, `PAGES_BASE` override, electron `./`, dev `/`).
2. A core-repo work item (`CG-…`) exists for the change, the core repository's own build and test gates pass, and the resulting core commit hash is recorded as a comment on this item.
3. A core-side test asserts that the scaffolded `vite.config.ts` production base equals the Pages project path (mirroring `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts` style).
4. The `core` submodule pointer in `tce-main-street` is bumped to the commit from AC 2, and `npm test` plus `npm run build` still pass in `tce-main-street` after the bump.
5. Re-running the scaffold against a fixture or a scratch checkout produces a `vite.config.ts` with the Pages base, proving the regression is closed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Raise the `CG-…` item in the core worklog and edit the scaffold template string.
- Add or extend the core-side scaffold test.
- Commit in core with the core item id, then `git -C core` is not used directly: bump the submodule pointer in `tce-main-street` and commit it here.

**Key Files:**
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — scaffold template gains the Pages base derivation.
- `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts` or `core/tests/scripts/` — core-side assert on the scaffolded base.
- `./.gitmodules` — unchanged URL; recorded only to document the HTTPS composition constraint.

**Dependencies:** `Production Pages build correctness` (the derivation being mirrored).

**Deliverables:** core template change committed under a `CG-…` item, core-side test, and the bumped submodule pointer here.

# GitHub Pages deploy workflow

**Parent:** MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 · `feature`

**Parent ACs covered:** 1 (auto-deploy on ship), 2 (Main Street only, with launcher), 4 (gated deployment), 5 (no stored SSH credentials), 9 (full project test suite passes).

**Goal.** Add `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` so every push to `main` runs the
quality gates and publishes `dist/` to GitHub Pages at
`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.

**Reuse.** Mirror `core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (same action versions,
`pages` concurrency group, `github-pages` environment, three-step configure /
upload / deploy) but drop the sibling-game composition step: this repo's
`./configs/game.json` preset already selects the core-owned Gym plus Main Street.

**Test-first.** The workflow contract test is written before the workflow file and
committed with it, so this item lands green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1.** Auto-deploy on ship: every push to `main` runs a GitHub Actions workflow that builds `tce-main-street` and deploys `dist/` to GitHub Pages at `https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.
- **2.** Gated deployment: the workflow runs unit tests and the production build first, and a failing test or build blocks deployment so no artefact is published.
- **3.** No stored SSH credentials: the build composes the `./core` submodule from the public core repo over HTTPS, needing no SSH secrets or `ssh-key` input.
- **4.** Main Street only (with launcher): the published site shows the launcher with exactly one playable example game, Main Street.
- **5.** The build uses the single-game preset and never `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, and no sibling `tce-<game>` repository is cloned, so no other example game can appear in the selector; the core-owned Gym is always present.
- **6.** Steps are ordered install (`npm ci`) → test (`npm test`) → build (`npm run build`) → `actions/configure-pages@v5` → `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` (`path: dist`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v4`, and no other trigger can publish unreleased work.
- **7.** `permissions` are exactly `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`; `concurrency` is `group: pages` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; the job uses `environment: github-pages` and exposes the deployed `page_url`.
- **8.** `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` parses the workflow YAML and asserts the trigger, step order, permissions, concurrency, the absence of secret/SSH references, and the absence of `GAMES_CONFIG=full`; the test fails if any of those are removed.
- **9.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes: `npm test` is green.
## Minimal Implementation

- Add `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` first (adapted from `core/tests/scripts/deploy-workflow.test.ts`).
- Add `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` with the steps, permissions and concurrency above.
- Confirm the submodule composition works from a clean checkout with no `ssh-key`.

**Key Files:**
- `./.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — **New.** Gated Pages build and deploy on `main`.
- `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` — **New.** Workflow wiring and secret-free contract test.
- `./.gitmodules` — governs the HTTPS submodule composition in CI.

**Dependencies:** `Pages base-path build tests`, `Production Pages build correctness`.

**Deliverables:** the deploy workflow plus its contract test, green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1.** Auto-deploy on ship, confirmed live: after the next `dev -> main` release the "Deploy to GitHub Pages" workflow run is green and its URL is recorded, proving every push to `main` runs the workflow that deploys `dist/` to GitHub Pages.
- **2.** Main Street only (with launcher), confirmed live: `https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/` shows the launcher with exactly one playable example game, Main Street, plus the core Gym, and no other `tce-<game>` is listed.
- **3.** Assets resolve under the Pages base path, confirmed live: Main Street starts and the console shows no 404s for the bundled JS/CSS entry, card art or audio; the entry script and at least one card-art and one audio URL return HTTP 200 under `/tce-main-street/`.
- **4.** The repository's Pages source is set to "GitHub Actions"; the settings location and the date the change was made are recorded as a comment on this item.
- **5.** Evidence is recorded on this item: live URL, workflow run URL, the console/network check result, and any deviation from the local reproduction documented in `./DEPLOYMENT.md`.
- **6.** If the live check fails, the failure is recorded and a blocking work item is raised rather than closing this item.
## Minimal Implementation

- Producer: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
- Agent: trigger (or wait for) the `main` deployment, then verify the live URL in a browser with the network console open.
- If the live check fails, record the failure and raise a blocking work item rather than closing this one.

**Key Files:**
- `./DEPLOYMENT.md` — the verification steps this item executes and validates.
- `./.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — the workflow run being verified.

**Dependencies:** `GitHub Pages deploy workflow`, `Deployment documentation`.

**Deliverables:** Pages enabled, a green production run, and recorded live-verification evidence.
